description: Streaming service subscription cancellations. Most streaming services have relatively easy cancellation but issues arise with free-trial-to-paid conversions, bundled packages, and continued charges.
typical_barriers: Free trial converted to paid without clear notice
Bundled with another service (e.g., phone plan)
Annual plan with no prorated refund

email_1.subject: Cancellation of Subscription — {{company_name}} — Account: {{account_identifier}}
key_points: If free-trial-to-paid issue, cite FTC rule and state ARL
Request confirmation and refund of unauthorized charges
Note date of original cancellation attempt if applicable

legal_citations.ca: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §17602(c) (free-trial-to-paid notice requirement)

email_3.subject: Final Notice: Subscription Cancellation — {{company_name}}
key_points: State intent to file complaint and dispute charges

apple_tv_plus.cancel_via: Settings > Apple ID > Subscriptions on iOS; or reportaproblem.apple.com for refunds
apple_tv_plus.notes: Managed through Apple subscription system, not the streaming service directly

subscriptions_via_app_store.cancel_via: Settings > Apple ID > Subscriptions on iOS device
subscriptions_via_app_store.notes: If subscribed through App Store, must cancel through Apple, not the service

subscriptions_via_google_play.notes: If subscribed through Google Play, must cancel through Google

notes: Streaming cancellations are usually lower-friction than gym or telecom, but free-trial-to-paid conversions and platform-mediated subscriptions (App Store/Play Store) create issues. Key point: if subscribed through Apple or Google, cancellation must go through them, not the streaming service.
